title: Weakly-Supervised Crack Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
mechanism: Refine coarse crack annotations by removing annotated pixels whose local visual features resemble the background (data-driven), replacing an earlier brightness-threshold refinement.
adaptation: Deliberately coarsen our crack labels to a 5 px band (covers 4 px FWHM plus 1 to 2 px jitter), then apply the data-driven refinement per cell so it adapts to each source's contrast; thin and re-dilate to source width. A second snapper to compare with the ridge snapper, expected to do better on low-contrast CSIR cracks.
min_experiment: Arm: house trained on coarsen-then-refine labels; baseline: house and the ridge-snap arm. Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2, CSIR crack relR@2. Kill if CSIR relR@2 not above the ridge-snap arm by 0.02 and pooled metrics n.d. vs house.
evidence: R: three crack segmentation datasets and one vessel dataset; annotation 10 to 30x faster at comparable detection accuracy (abstract).
prior_overlap: none: no label refinement was run (BRIEF section 5, Labels row).
